accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core L.1.1c (use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences, e.g. He hops; We hop) and L.3.1f (ensure subject-verb and pronoun-antecedent agreement), and the DfE (2013) English programmes of study, English Appendix 2 (Year 1 regular plural noun suffixes -s/-es; Year 2 grammar terms noun, verb; Year 4 Standard English verb inflections such as we were, not we was). The lesson states the rule exactly as English marks it in the present tense: only a third-person singular subject takes the -s/-es suffix, while I, you, we, they and plural nouns take the base form. Be (I am, he is, they are) and have (she has, they have) are given as irregular forms, and -es after s, sh, ch and x matches standard spelling rules. Compound subjects joined by and are plural.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented agreement errors in young writers: s on both noun and verb (the s swap prediction 'The frogs hops', 'both' tag, m9), s after I ('I rides my bike' prediction, 'i' tag, m3), is after two names joined by and (Tom and Ana prediction, 'and' tag, m4), s after irregular plurals (The children plays in Fix it, 'irr' tag, m5), the misspelling washs ('es' tag, m6), and an -ing verb used without a helper ('ing' tag). Finding the subject first is the fix taught in every step.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsva is built on the single moving s: one draggable s tile that the child places on either the noun slot or the verb slot as the picture changes between one animal and several, so the trade-off (only one word gets the s) is physical. Other steps tap the subject (word tiles gain subject/verb role labels), fill a verb blank under a pronoun picture, choose is or are, and tap the one wrong verb to fix it. Shingle similarity is 11.5% with flag_blend.js, 8.1% with flag_sorry.js, 8.0% with flag_poss.js and lower with every other lab, including the tense and determiner/pronoun labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule by moving it: with one cat the s only fits on naps, with three frogs dropping it on hop gives 'Only one word gets the s' and it must go on frogs. Pronoun pictures (one child, two children, the child pointing at self) make he, they and I concrete before the rule is named, and the Fix it step shows the corrected sentence with the reason ('Sam and Mia are two people, so no s: run'). Done lines restate the rule and quote the child's prediction.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the next task tests: 'The frogs hops' (the s swap shows only one s fits), 'I rides my bike' (the I step gives ride), and 'is, Ana is one girl' for Tom and Ana (the is/are step counts two people). A.reveal quotes the child's own pick in each done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() names the slip for each: both ('Only one word gets the s. Many dogs: the dogs run'), one ('One person or thing: add s to the verb'), i ('I and you never take the s: I walk'), irr ('Children already means more than one'), and ('Two names joined by and make more than one. Use are'), es ('After sh, ch, s or x, add es: washes'), ing ('An ing word needs a helper') and am ('Am only goes with I'). Wrong taps inside the lab also explain themselves.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 0.2 in short concrete sentences ('One dog runs. Two dogs run.'). Adult text measures FK 7.4 and uses the precise terms subject, verb, singular, plural, present tense, -s/-es suffix, pronoun, agreement and Standard English, with L.1.1c, L.3.1f and the English Appendix 2 references.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 0.2%. Kid paragraphs cover subject and verb, the one-s rule, pronouns and is/are; adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, the key terms and irregular forms, five named mistakes with a check routine, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for every step: word tiles (48 px tall, wrapping onto a second line for longer sentences with the full stop kept beside the last word), the dashed s slots, the s tray and the two big button twins (frog + s, hop + s) fit the width; pictures sit above the sentence; young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console errors. A manual probe dragged the s to the noun slot for three frogs ('The frogs hop.') and to the verb slot for one cat ('The cat naps.'). Every drag and tap has a button twin, and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.
